paper_metadata.title: Diffusion bonding of the high temperature Ti alloy IMI 829 to Fe-Ni alloy IN 907 using interlayers

evidence.quote: the Ti alloy IMI 829, capable of operation at a tem-perature of 540°C has been used as the substrate for the diffusion bonding of a more wear resistant surface.
The wear resistant surface was the Fe-Ni alloy IN 907, which has a similar coefficient of thermal ex-pansion to the IMI 829
IMI Titanium Ltd. supplied the IMI 829 (wt% Ti-5.5A1-3.5Sn-3.OZr-l.ONb-0.3Mo-0.3Si) in the form of 4.8 mm thick sheet
IMI 829 as received: 660 MPa, after DB thermal cycle 975°C for 1 h: 654 MPa
IN 907 as received: 774 MPa, after DB thermal cycle 975°C for 1 h: 634 MPa
The diffusion bonding was carried out in a vacuum hot press using platen pressure in a vacuum of x 5 x lop6 Torr.

attributes.location: reaction zone between Ta and Ni interlayers

evidence.quote: the reaction zone between the Ta and Ni interlayers was visible optically (Fig. 6) and X-ray diffraction suggested that it was primarily of Ni,Ta
Stabilis-ation of the B phase in the IMI 829 had occurred at the interface.
The IMI 829 showed a typical B heat treated mi-crostructure, which was not changed by the DB.

attributes.size: ~85 um after 925C/1h; 175 um after 925C/4h; ~146 um after 975C/1h

evidence.quote: The total width of the reaction zone was x 85 urn after DB at 925°C for 1 h but increased to 175 urn after 925°C for 4 h. After DB at 975°C for 1 h the total reaction zone width was x 146 pm.
the reaction zone at the interface between the Nb-44 wt% Ti or Ti- 15 wt% MO interlayers and the IN 907 was much reduced to only = 15 pm thick.

attributes.morphology: mainly intergranular with some ductile failure in Ta interlayer

evidence.quote: The shear fracture surface of the joint with Ta and Ni interlay-ers was mainly intergranular in nature, where frac-ture had occurred through the Ni,Ta reaction zone but also with some evidence of ductile failure in the Ta interlayer
Some porosity was seen at the bond interfaces.
